simple: A machine that follows a list of exact steps to work with information.
analogy: A cook who follows a recipe word for word.
precise: A machine that carries out a stored list of instructions, one at a time, on data such as numbers and letters.
source: D1 of F0-01, D2 of F0-01 (pending verification: title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: One single step that tells the machine to do one thing.
analogy: One line of a recipe, like "crack the egg".
precise: One command that a computer can carry out; a program is made of many of them.
source: D2 of F0-01 (pending verification: title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: A list of clear steps that solves a problem, every time.
analogy: A recipe that always makes the same dish if you follow it exactly.
precise: A finite list of exact steps that, followed in order, solves a problem. It can be written in words, drawn, or written as a program.
source: D1 of F0-01 (pending verification: title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: An algorithm written in a language a computer can follow.
analogy: The recipe, translated into the cook's own language.
precise: A list of instructions written in a programming language, such as C++, that is turned into instructions the computer can carry out.
source: D2 of F0-01, D3 of F0-01 (pending verification: title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: The smallest piece of information: on or off, 1 or 0.
analogy: One light switch.
precise: A binary digit, which has exactly one of two values, written 0 and 1.
source: D1 of F0-02 (pending verification: title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: A way of writing numbers using only the two digits 0 and 1.
analogy: A row of switches where each switch is worth double the one to its right.
precise: The base-2 number system: each position has a place value that is a power of two (1, 2, 4, 8 and so on).
source: D1 of F0-02 (pending verification: title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: How much a digit is worth because of where it sits.
analogy: The price tag stuck under each switch.
precise: The number a position stands for; in our usual decimal numbers the places are 1, 10, 100; in binary they are 1, 2, 4, 8 and so on.
source: D1 of F0-02 (pending verification: title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: A group of eight bits.
analogy: A row of eight light switches.
precise: A unit of eight bits; it can hold 256 different patterns, so one byte can stand for a whole number from 0 to 255.
source: D1 of F0-02 (pending verification: title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: An agreement about which number stands for which thing.
analogy: Jun and Priya's "A is 1, B is 2" note on the fridge.
precise: A fixed rule that matches each symbol (a letter, a colour, a sound level) with a pattern of bits, so both writer and reader get the same meaning. Not the same as "code" meaning a program's text.
source: D1 of F0-03 (pending verification: title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: A table that gives every letter, digit and sign its own number.
analogy: The fridge note, but agreed by the whole world.
precise: A mapping from characters to numbers. ASCII (American Standard Code for Information Interchange) is an early example; Unicode is a larger one for the writing systems of the world.
source: D1 of F0-03 (pending verification: title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: One tiny dot of a picture.
analogy: One tile in a mosaic on a kitchen wall.
precise: A picture element: one point of an image, stored as numbers that describe its colour.
source: D1 of F0-03 (pending verification: title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: One measurement of a sound at one moment.
analogy: One frame of a flip book.
precise: A number that records the level of a sound wave at one instant; a recording is a long list of samples taken at regular times.
source: D1 of F0-03 (pending verification: title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: Putting things in order, like smallest to biggest.
analogy: Lining up cards in your hand from low to high.
precise: Rearranging a list so that each item is no bigger than the next one (or no smaller, for the other direction).
source: D2 of F0-04 (pending verification: title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: Looking at two things and deciding which is bigger.
analogy: Holding two cards side by side.
precise: A test between two values whose answer is yes or no, such as "is the left one bigger than the right one?". Counting comparisons is one way to measure how much work a sorting method does.
source: D2 of F0-04 (pending verification: title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: Two things change places.
analogy: Two children in a line trading spots.
precise: Exchanging the values in two positions of a list.
source: D2 of F0-04 (pending verification: title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: A fixed plan of "compare these two, swap if needed" stations that always sorts.
analogy: A chalk path on the floor where people meet at boxes, compare, and step left or right.
precise: A fixed sequence of compare-and-swap operations on fixed positions, chosen so that any starting order comes out sorted.
source: R1 of F0-04 (lab run in this build: all 24 starting orders sorted); the name itself is pending an algorithms textbook in the registry

simple: The part that carries out the program's steps.
analogy: The head chef.
precise: The processor: the circuit that fetches instructions from memory and carries them out, one after another, working on data. A CPU can contain one or more cores; each core is like one head chef.
source: D1 of F0-05, D3 of F0-05 (pending verification: title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: A tiny place inside the CPU that holds a number it is working on right now.
analogy: The chef's hands and the cutting board.
precise: A small, very fast storage place inside the processor that holds one value; instructions work on values in registers.
source: D1 of F0-05 (pending verification: title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: A small, fast store near the CPU for things used often.
analogy: Shelves near the stove.
precise: A small, fast memory between the processor and main memory that keeps copies of recently used data, so it can be reached sooner.
source: D3 of F0-05 (pending verification: title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: The big workspace that holds the program and its data while it runs.
analogy: The big pantry down the corridor.
precise: The computer's large working memory (built from DRAM chips, dynamic random-access memory), where running programs and their data are kept; its contents are lost when the power goes off.
source: D3 of F0-05 (pending verification: title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: Where files and programs are kept, even when the computer is off.
analogy: The warehouse across town.
precise: A device such as an SSD (solid-state drive) or a hard disk that keeps data without power; it is larger and slower to reach than main memory.
source: D3 of F0-05 (pending verification: title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: The paths that carry information between the parts.
analogy: Corridors and service lifts.
precise: A set of connections that carries data, addresses and control signals between the processor, memory and devices.
source: D2 of F0-05 (pending verification: title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: Information coming into the computer, and results going out.
analogy: Order slips through the order window; plates out through the serving hatch.
precise: The transfer of data between the computer and the outside world through devices such as a keyboard (input) or a screen (output).
source: D2 of F0-05 (pending verification: title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: Information that goes into the computer.
analogy: What your ears and eyes take in.
precise: Data that a program receives from outside itself, for example from a keyboard, a mouse, a microphone, a sensor or a file.
source: D1 of F0-06 (pending verification: title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: Information or action that comes out of the computer.
analogy: Your voice and your hands.
precise: Data or signals that a program sends out, for example to a screen, a speaker, a printer, a lamp, a motor or a file.
source: D1 of F0-06 (pending verification: title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: The work the computer does between the input and the output.
analogy: Your thinking: "the bell rang, so it is Grandma".
precise: The steps of the program that turn input data into output data.
source: D2 of F0-06 (pending verification: title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: A part that measures something about the world, like light or heat, and turns it into a number.
analogy: One of your senses.
precise: A device that responds to a physical quantity (light, temperature, sound, movement) and produces a signal that the computer can read as a value.
source: D3 of F0-06 (pending verification: title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: A piece of equipment connected to the computer.
analogy: A tool or helper in the house.
precise: A hardware unit that the computer communicates with, such as a keyboard, screen or sensor.
source: D1 of F0-06 (pending verification: title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: A question whose answer is yes or no.
analogy: "Is the cup full?"
precise: An expression that is either true or false, used to decide which step comes next.
source: D1 of F0-07 (pending verification: title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: A step that chooses what to do, using a yes-or-no question.
analogy: "If it is too hot, wait one minute."
precise: A branch in an algorithm: if the condition is true, one set of steps runs; otherwise another set (or nothing) runs. In C++ it is written with if and else.
source: D1 of F0-07, D3 of F0-07 (pending verification: title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: Steps that are repeated.
analogy: "Stir 20 times."
precise: A part of an algorithm that runs again and again, either a set number of times or while a condition stays true. In C++, for and while make loops.
source: D1 of F0-07, D3 of F0-07 (pending verification: title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: A loop that never stops.
analogy: "Add milk until the cup is full", but nobody ever adds milk.
precise: A loop whose condition never becomes false, usually because nothing inside the loop changes what the condition tests.
source: D1 of F0-07 (pending verification: title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: The extra 1 you pass to the next column when a column adds up to too much.
analogy: When 9 + 3 = 12, you write 2 and "carry the 1".
precise: The value moved into the next place when the sum of one place is at least the base (10 in decimal, 2 in binary).
source: D2 of F0-07 (pending verification: title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: A mistake that makes a program do the wrong thing.
analogy: A mistake in the recipe.
precise: A fault in a program (or in the data, the hardware or another program it depends on) that makes it behave differently from what was intended.
source: D1 of F0-08 (pending verification: title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: Finding and fixing bugs.
analogy: Hana checking the recipe and the jars.
precise: The process of locating the cause of a wrong behaviour, correcting it, and checking that the correction works.
source: D1 of F0-08 (pending verification: title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: What you notice is wrong.
analogy: "the bread is flat and salty".
precise: An observable sign of a fault, such as wrong output, a crash or a program that never ends; it is not the cause itself.
source: D1 of F0-08 (pending verification: title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: The real reason behind the symptom.
analogy: The swapped jar labels.
precise: The underlying fault that, once fixed, makes the symptom go away and stay away.
source: D1 of F0-08 (pending verification: title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: A small try that checks if something works.
analogy: Tasting a pinch from each jar.
precise: Running a program (or part of it) with chosen inputs and comparing what it does with what it should do.
source: D1 of F0-08 (pending verification: title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: A mistake where something happens one time too many or one time too few.
analogy: Stirring 19 times when the recipe says 20.
precise: A bug in which a count, a limit or a position is wrong by exactly one, often from choosing "less than" instead of "less than or equal".
source: D2 of F0-08 (pending verification: title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: Computers joined together so they can send each other messages.
analogy: The postal service, with post offices and roads between them.
precise: A set of computers and connecting devices, linked by cables or radio, that pass data from one computer to another.
source: D1 of F0-09 (pending verification: title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: One small piece of a message that travels on its own.
analogy: One postcard of Ines's story.
precise: A unit of data sent across a network, made of a header (with information such as the addresses) and a piece of the message.
source: D1 of F0-09 (pending verification: title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: The number or name that says which computer a packet is for, and which sent it.
analogy: The address written on a postcard, and the sender's name.
precise: An identifier of a computer (or a part of one) on a network, carried in each packet so it can be delivered, and so the reply can find its way back.
source: D1 of F0-09 (pending verification: title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: Agreed rules for how computers talk.
analogy: Ines and Tomás agreeing to write "card n of 5" and to ask for missing cards.
precise: A set of rules that sender and receiver both follow: what a message looks like, in what order things are sent, and what to do when something goes wrong.
source: D1 of F0-09 (pending verification: title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: A box that passes packets along towards where they are going.
analogy: A post office that sorts postcards and sends each one onwards.
precise: A network device that receives packets and forwards each one towards its destination address.
source: D1 of F0-09 (pending verification: title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: A machine with a computer inside that senses the world and moves in it by itself.
analogy: A body with senses, a brain and muscles.
precise: A machine that uses sensors, a computer running a program, and actuators to act in the physical world, following that program rather than direct moment-by-moment human control.
source: D1 of F0-10 (pending verification: title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: A flying robot, often with spinning propellers.
analogy: A body that must keep its balance in the air all the time.
precise: An unmanned aircraft; a multirotor drone uses a computer (the flight controller) that reads its sensors and changes the speed of its motors to stay balanced and move.
source: D3 of F0-10 (pending verification: title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: A part that makes something move or happen.
analogy: A muscle.
precise: A device that turns a command from the computer into a physical action, such as a motor turning a wheel.
source: D1 of F0-10 (pending verification: title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: A part that spins when it gets electricity.
analogy: The muscle that turns a wheel or a propeller.
precise: An electric machine that turns electrical energy into turning motion; the most common actuator in small robots and drones.
source: D2 of F0-10 (pending verification: title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: The robot's repeating cycle: sense, think, act, and again.
analogy: Amira's "feel, decide, move" in the dark hallway.
precise: A loop in which a program reads sensors, decides on commands from what it read, sends the commands to the actuators, and repeats, so that each action is based on fresh measurements.
source: D1 of F0-10, D4 of F0-10 (pending verification: title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: A program that pretends to be the real world, so you can test a robot safely.
analogy: Practising a dance in your room before the show.
precise: Software that models a robot and its surroundings well enough to run the robot's program and observe what would happen, without real hardware.
source: D1 of F0-10 (pending verification: title only, dossier gate G1 open)
